name: St. Abda of Dair-Koni
bio:
Abda of Dair-Koni, known in Classical Syriac as Marya Abda, was a priest and abbot of the Church of the East in the early centuries of Christian witness in Mesopotamia. His name, meaning "servant," fittingly describes a life given over to the discipline of the desert and the care of souls entrusted to him.

As abbot he governed a monastic community at Dair-Koni, guiding his monks in prayer, manual labor, and the chanting of the Psalms. The monasteries of the Syriac tradition were nurseries of holiness and learning, and Abda's rule shaped a generation of ascetics who carried the Gospel eastward.

Though the details of his life are sparse, his memory endured among the Christian communities of the region, who honored him as a faithful shepherd and a man of prayer. He stands as a quiet witness to the deep roots of monastic Christianity in the lands between the rivers.

prayer.text: O God, who called Your servant Abda to the solitude of the desert and entrusted to him the care of a monastic household, grant through his intercession that we may serve You with undivided heart and lead others to Your truth. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.
